images.title: Same corner, other crossing
images.purpose: Show that corresponding angles sit in the same corner at the two crossings.
images.composition: The same two-lines-and-transversal figure, with only one corresponding pair emphasised and the rest faint.
exact_structure: Two horizontal grey (#6B7280) lines l above and m below, and one slanting dark line t crossing both.
At the crossing with l, the top left angle is filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) and numbered 1.
At the crossing with m, the top left angle is filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) and numbered 5.
A dashed grey arrow runs down along t from angle 1 to angle 5.
The other six angles are drawn only as thin grey arcs with no number and no fill.
A short caption sits at the right side beside the dashed arrow.
rejection: any of the other six angles filled or numbered
1 and 5 in different corners (for example 5 at the bottom right)
images.takeaway: Corresponding angles are in the same corner at the two crossings.
images.description: Angles 1 and 5 filled in the top left corner of each crossing, joined by a dashed arrow.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students point to the corner, then slide down t to the matching corner.

image_decisions.why: Highlighting a single corresponding pair keeps the picture clear.
